spec: WIRE_SPEC sections 3.1 (bundle fields), 3.7 (transcript v6, KDF, KCMAC, frame keys), 3.7.4 (SAS commitment and REVEAL), 3.8 (DTLS certificate binding) and 4 (SAS v6)
description: Deterministic KAT for the signed 1:1 handshake v6 (caller SAS commitment + REVEAL) with the DTLS fingerprint binding. Generated by scripts/handshake-v6-kat-dump.mjs with node:crypto + pure Ed25519. Every consumer pins this file's sha256. sigV6 is deterministic RFC 8032; a verifier that cannot reproduce signature bytes (CryptoKit) verifies the golden signature instead. The vectors named design-check carry the values of the independent Python reference of the design.

commit.layout: sasCommit = SHA-256("qaudion-sas-commit-v6" (21 bytes ASCII, not length-prefixed) || LP(callId) || sasNonce[32]); LP = u16 BE length || UTF-8; sasCommitB64 = standard base64 with padding of the 32 raw bytes.

transcripts.layout: WIRE_SPEC 3.7: OFFER_v6 / ACCEPT_v6; OFFER_v6 ends with DTLSFP_offerer[33] || LP(sasCommit | empty) (32 B in round 1, empty in rounds >= 2); ACCEPT_v6 ends with DTLSFP_acceptor[33] and binds the commitment through offerBinding = SHA-256(OFFER_v6)

kdf.layout: sessionKey = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = pqcSS || x25519SS, salt = psk | "q-audion-hybrid-pqc-v1", info = "q-audion-session-key" || SHA-256(ACCEPT_v6), 32); KCMAC per KeyConfirmation (offer/accept bindings = SHA-256(OFFER_v6) / SHA-256(ACCEPT_v6)). The SAS is in the sas section: the nonce never enters these.

sas.layout: SAS-KDF = HKDF-SHA256(IKM = sessionKey of round 1, salt = "qaudion-sas-v1", info = "q-audion-sas-v6" (15 B) || SHA-256(ACCEPT_v6 of round 1) || sasNonce, L = 18); idx[i] = ((out[3i] << 16) | (out[3i+1] << 8) | out[3i+2]) mod 256, i = 0..5; words = PGP even-word list[idx[i]]

frameKeys.description: frameKey_o2a / frameKey_a2o = HKDF-SHA256(IKM = sessionKey, salt = "qaudion-frame-salt-v5", info = "q-audion-frame-key-v5:" || callId || ":o2a" | ":a2o", L = 32). o = offerer (caller, signer of OFFER_v6), a = acceptor. The labels keep the -v5 names: they name the frame-key scheme, which v6 does not change.

reveal.layout: data = <callId>|SASREVEAL:<B>; B = canonical base64 (padding, standard alphabet, 88 characters) of acceptBinding[32] || sasNonce[32]; the whole data is at most 200 characters. Callee order: route (callId prefix, case-sensitive SASREVEAL:) -> parse B (else sas_commit_mismatch) -> acceptBinding == own acceptHash (else sibling) -> SHA-256(label || LP(callId) || nonce) == storedCommit (else sas_commit_mismatch). expect: ok | sas_commit_mismatch | sibling | drop. In every vector callId is the call the receiving device is in.

bundle.layout: JSON bundle as sent in <callId>|{json}. expect: ok (parses and passes the structural checks of WIRE_SPEC 3.1; the signature is not evaluated here) or handshake_malformed (WIRE_SPEC 3.8.6). transcriptVector names the transcript vector whose values the signed fields carry.

sequences.layout: See the comment block of scripts/handshake-v6-kat-dump.mjs and WIRE_SPEC 3.7.4: events are abstract; arg values are ids of vectors in this file. A platform replays them against its own handshake/controller seam and checks every non-null expect field.

negative.description: Same inputs as transcript vector v6-basic-no-psk, no PSK. In each case one leg sees a different DTLS fingerprint or a different sasCommit (a MITM on both legs, signatures stripped): that leg derives a different OFFER_v6 hash, ACCEPT_v6 hash, session key and SAS, so no media decrypts and the KCMAC fails.
